title: The dragon’s masks; folded breastplate; fear around the teeth
english: … these actors on the stage: sometimes the masks of governors, sometimes of other kings, sometimes of women. Their own face is hidden, and what they are does not show; what they seem to be is what people see. The dragon is like that. He never shows his own face; but if he has taken on a face to deceive people, that is the one he uses. And this enemy certainly has many masks, and for each vice he takes on a face of virtue.

And a little later, on what follows, the rest of the verse written above: The face he has put on, who is able to expose it? Who is able to uncover it and [show] what the dragon is within? Such too are certain others, his disciples, “who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves” (Matthew 7:15).

“And who could get inside the fold of his breastplate?” (Job 41:13). Do you see? This is called a breastplate, and a chest; and the breastplate is where the ruling faculty is. His breastplate is not simple. He has nothing simple about him. He is crafty; he is folded over. So who could get inside the fold of his breastplate? A saint can expose him and show that his breastplate is folded over; but the saint's own breastplate is not folded.

“Who will open the gates of his face?” (Job 41:14). He hides the things stored up within. So who will open the gates of his face? Who is the one able to expose him and to show how much deceit, how much venom, how many evils he keeps stored up?

“Around his teeth is fear” (Job 41:14). Of these teeth it is said, “You have broken the teeth of sinners” (Psalm 3:7), and, “The Lord will crush the molars of the lions” (Psalm 58:6). This fear is not the fear of God; it is the fear that is around his teeth. But if you have Christ within yourself, pay no heed to this …

title: Asp-hard insides; burning lamps from the mouth; power in the neck
english: … fear. For “you shall fear the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 6:13), and apart from him do not fear any other.

“His insides are bronze asps” (Job 41:15). These are his teachings, his hidden thoughts. Everything is the venom of asps, everything that is inside him. And they are not some soft asps but hard ones; for the asps are hard.
“From his mouth” (Job 41:19): the blasphemies and the words of ungodly and godless teachers.

“From his mouth go out burning torches, and braziers of fire are flung about” (Job 41:19). I think, for my part, that all the ungodly who bring in godless doctrines would properly be members of the dragon. And if you want to hear the names of the dragon's members, who are they? The dragon's mouth may also be something understood figuratively, and with it the place from which the destroying words come. [For from his mouth torches of fire perish.] Because from his mouth braziers of fire perish.

If I ever heard a speech that accused the Creator under the pretext of Christianity, a speech, say, championing the teachings of Marcion, championing those of Valentinus and of Basilides; when they speak ill of the Maker of heaven and earth, when they say that he is not, and is not of spiritual substance either, the sort of things these men say: you will see that from the mouth of such people burning torches go out and braziers of fire are flung about. That is why we, who know this, should keep watch over ourselves, so that those torches never burn us and the braziers of fire never touch us.

“And in his neck power makes its home” (Job 41:22). There is a certain wicked power. But the weakness that my Saviour and Lord took on for my sake, which is called the weakness of God, has conquered …

title: God’s weakness stronger than the dragon; Job’s double reward
english: … that one's power. For the weakness of God, the Apostle says, is “stronger than men” (1 Corinthians 1:25); but I would say: stronger than the power of the dragon.

“And the pieces of flesh of his body are glued together” (Job 41:23). He could have said, “The pieces of flesh of his body are united.” But he did not say it, for they are not united; that is not so. With him, the one is many; or else things that seem to be one are glued together, as the one who says “are glued,” not “are united,” shows.

“His heart is set fast like a stone; it stands like an anvil that cannot be beaten out” (Job 41:24). He is not beaten out, he does not follow the word; [by his own nature] he is hard, not to be beaten out, unyielding. And if anyone has drawn power from the devil, from this dragon, he too has the heart that cannot be beaten out and is not beaten out. But if someone is gold, he follows the Word, the [goldsmith]; and so he yields, until he becomes a leaf of gold and receives the impressions of the letters of God, in Christ Jesus, to whom be the glory for ever. Amen.

“And the Lord gave double, as much as Job had before, doubling it” (Job 42:10). The noble athlete who underwent every trial, Job, most courageous of men, receives the prizes of his endurance, as the Scripture says: everything double compared with what he had before. But the Lord Jesus Christ gives prizes not double but a hundredfold. For he says: “Whoever leaves father or mother, house, brothers, sisters, for my sake or for the sake of the Gospel,” as is written in the Gospel according to Mark, “will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life” (Mark 10:29-30). He would not have received double of what he had before if he had not shown double the virtue.
